dedupe_keys.name: secom semiconductor manufacturing process dataset uci

description: SECOM is a dataset of semiconductor manufacturing process measurements in which each of 1,567 examples is one production entity with 591 sensor and process features and a pass or fail label from in-house line testing. It is intended for classification and causal discovery, in particular for finding which signals matter most for production yield through feature selection. It was donated to the UCI Machine Learning Repository by Michael McCann and Adrian Johnston on 18 November 2008. Coverage is a single, unnamed production line, with anonymised features. The data are free to download from UCI under a CC BY 4.0 licence and citable through DOI 10.24432/C54305. Caveats: many features contain missing values coded as NaN, the features are anonymised, so physical interpretation is not possible and results may not transfer to other fabs. For simulation it is a benchmark for fault detection and yield prediction methods that feed condition monitoring in manufacturing digital twins and resilience studies of chip supply. It is related to the TON_IoT and Edge-IIoTset records in this catalogue, which provide industrial sensor data for security, not quality.
